1.title: Pull the house wires out
1.say: Twist the small twist caps off the wires in the wall box, so the bare ends are open. Gently pull the two white wires and the two black wires out from the box, so you can reach each bare end.
placements: small twist caps on house wire ends → twisted counterclockwise off and set aside away from wall box (in the video: two orange caps held at right side of frame)
two white house wires with bare ends → pulled forward to hang free out of wall box left and right (in the video: left edge and right side of gray box opening)
two black house wires with bare ends → pulled forward to hang free out of wall box top and middle (in the video: top center and middle right of gray box opening)
watch_for: if fewer than four bare ends show, a wire is still folded inside the box
if copper looks cut or broken, you pulled too hard so stop and straighten it
1.check_yourself: It should look like four bare wire ends sticking out of the wall box with no caps on.
1.safety: Switch the heater breaker off and keep it off, so no power reaches the box.

2.title: Check the wires have no power
2.say: Touch both probe tips of the tester to bare wire ends in the box, so the tester can show any power. Test each black wire against each white wire, so you know every pair is dead before you touch them.
placements: tester's first probe tip → touched to bare end of black house wire inside wall box (in the video: middle black wire at center of gray box)
tester's second probe tip → touched to bare copper bundle at bottom of wall box (in the video: bottom edge of gray box opening with tester body at right)
watch_for: if the tester lights or beeps, power is still on so stop and switch the breaker off
if you test only one pair, another wire could still be live so test every mix
2.check_yourself: It should look like the tester tips touching the bare wires with no light or sound showing power.
2.safety: Keep your fingers on the plastic handles only, so bare metal never touches your skin.

3.title: Join the white wires together
3.say: Twist the two white house wires together with your fingers, so the bare copper ends wind around each other. Screw a small twist cap tightly onto the twisted white ends, so no copper shows outside the cap. Push the capped white wires deep to the back of the box, so only the two black wires hang out front.
placements: two white house wires → twisted together with fingers with about one centimetre of bare ends winding (in the video: center of gray box opening)
small twist cap for white wires → screwed clockwise over twisted ends until tight with no copper showing (in the video: yellow cap pushed to back wall of gray box)
capped white wires → pushed deep to back inside bottom of wall box (in the video: bottom back corner of gray box leaving two black wires out front)
watch_for: if copper shows below the cap, the cap is loose so twist it tighter
if a white wire pulls out when you tug, the twist was loose so retwist them
3.check_yourself: It should look like two black wires hanging out with the capped white wires hidden deep inside the box.
3.safety: Keep the breaker off while you twist, so a live wire cannot shock you.

4.title: Join first black to thermostat
4.say: Hold one short thermostat wire beside the first black house wire, so the bare ends line up together. Twist a small twist cap over both bare ends until tight, so the thermostat hangs from that first joint.
placements: first black house wire on left → lined side by side with one short wire from back of hanging thermostat (in the video: left side of gray box opening)
small twist cap for first joint → screwed clockwise over both bare ends until tight with thermostat hanging down (in the video: red cap just outside top left of gray box)
watch_for: if copper shows under the cap, the cap is not tight so twist further
if you join both house wires to one thermostat wire, keep the second black free
4.check_yourself: It should look like the thermostat hanging by one capped joint with one black house wire still free.
4.safety: Keep the breaker off while you join the wires, so you stay clear of shock.

5.title: Join second black to thermostat
5.say: Hold the last free black house wire beside the last free thermostat wire, so the bare ends meet side by side. Twist a small twist cap over both bare ends until snug, so both joints hang and support the thermostat.
placements: second black house wire on right → lined side by side with last free short wire from back of hanging thermostat (in the video: right side of gray box opening near top)
small twist cap for second joint → screwed clockwise over both bare ends until snug with no copper showing (in the video: red cap just outside top of gray box beside first cap)
watch_for: if you join black to white, the heater will not work so use black to black only
if the cap feels loose when you tug, retwist until no copper shows
5.check_yourself: It should look like the thermostat hanging from the box by two capped black joints.
5.safety: Keep the breaker off for the second joint too, so neither black wire can shock you.

6.title: Screw thermostat flat to wall
6.say: Fold the capped wires gently back into the wall box, so the base can sit flat over the opening. Hold the thermostat base with the knob facing you over the box, so it covers the opening flat. Drive the top screw and the bottom screw snug, so the base does not wobble.
placements: capped wire joints → folded gently inside wall box behind thermostat (in the video: inside center of gray box)
thermostat base with center knob facing forward → centered flat over rectangular wall opening covering wall box (in the video: black base centered on white wall over gray box)
top mounting screw and bottom mounting screw → driven with driver into top and bottom tabs of wall box until snug (in the video: top center and bottom center of black base)
watch_for: if the base rocks, wires are trapped behind so refold them deeper
if the base sits crooked, the screws are uneven so loosen and straighten it
6.check_yourself: It should look like the thermostat base with the knob sitting flat and straight over the wall opening.
6.safety: Keep fingers clear of the spinning driver tip, so it cannot catch your skin.

7.title: Push the cover onto thermostat
7.say: Line up the cover with the base on the wall, so the knob pokes through the center hole. Push the cover straight in until it clicks, so it sits flat against the wall.
placements: outer cover with center dial hole → pushed straight onto thermostat base centered on wall until click (in the video: white square cover centered on white wall over black base)
watch_for: if the cover gaps from the wall, the knob is misaligned so lift and realign it
if it will not click, the base is pushed out so press the base flatter
7.check_yourself: It should look like a square cover with a center dial sitting flat and centered on the wall.
